currentContext.strengths: Global scale leadership: one of the largest global producers of food-grade iron phosphate by production capacity, with total annual manufacturing capacity of 1,33,000 MT including the upcoming greenfield facility|First-mover regulatory franchise: first and only company in India, and one of few worldwide, to hold USFDA approval for manufacture of mineral-based food ingredients|Regulatory moat: only company in India and one of nine globally to hold a Certificate of Suitability (CEP) from the Council of Europe for calcium carbonate as an API|Enduring customer relationships: 1,120+ customers including 14 Fortune 500 companies and 40+ blue-chip multinationals; average relationship with the five largest customers runs close to seven years|Technology platform: six proprietary in-house technologies (encapsulation, spray drying, granulation, trituration, liposomal preparations, precision blending) underpinning application-specific formulation solutions|R&D depth: 41 scientists/technical professionals, 420+ R&D projects undertaken, 127 products commercialised
currentContext.strategies: Deepen position in regulated nutrition via the NSS Ireland acquisition, giving a European manufacturing base, advanced premix capability and proximity to customers.|Move up the value curve in mineral science via the Nandesari greenfield and the Specialty Ingredients vertical (e.g., AbsorBis Bisglycinates, Lipoboost liposomal ingredients), shifting from supplying ingredients to solving customer formulation problems.|Extend mineral chemistry into electrification through Sudeep Advanced Materials, applying a decade of iron-phosphate experience to battery-grade material via a proprietary, lower-effluent process, aimed at a reliable source outside China.|Move closer to the customer: established warehousing in the US and Europe to shorten lead times, and is engaging select customer segments directly rather than through distributors.|Building leadership depth across science, manufacturing, regulatory affairs, quality and commercial functions by developing internal talent and hiring experienced professionals as the business expands.|Strengthening risk management and diversifying markets to manage execution risk while ramping new capacity and commercialising new technologies.|Sizing the Battery Materials business to validated, visible customer demand rather than anticipated demand, a discipline management says will not change as it scales.|The Board recommended declaring a dividend for FY 2025-26 to be paid out of the Company's profits, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. The Company maintains a Code of Conduct and governance framework under which the Board reviews strategy, business plans, annual operating and capital expenditure budgets, and risk management as standing agenda items at every meeting, and the Audit Committee reviews related-party transactions and internal financial controls as part of its oversight.
currentContext.expansion: The Company completed its IPO and listed on the BSE and NSE on 28th November, 2025, providing a capital framework to support aggressive global expansion and entry into the energy materials sector. The Nandesari Greenfield (Unit IV) - the Company's largest facility to date, adding 51,200 MT of annual capacity for pharmaceutical excipients and next-generation molecules (bisglycinates, gluconates, citrates) - had construction nearly complete during the year; it completed internal validation and qualification and is now in the customer validation phase. Commissioning was delayed by LPG and energy supply constraints, which have since been worked through, with commercial production expected to ramp through the second half of FY 2026-27 into FY 2027-28. In May 2025 the Company acquired an 85% stake in Nutrition Supplies and Services (NSS), an Ireland-based infant and medical nutrition premix specialist, through Sudeep Pharma B.V., giving immediate entry into regulated European infant and clinical nutrition markets and bypassing typical 4-to-7-year regulatory approval cycles; Sudeep India is beginning to act as NSS's primary ingredient supplier. Through subsidiary Sudeep Advanced Materials (SAMPL/SAM), the Company entered the battery materials market (precursor cathode active material for LFP batteries), breaking ground on a plant at Dahej, Gujarat (spread across 80,980 sq. metres) on 23rd January 2026; Phase I capacity of 25,000 MT is targeted for commissioning by Q1 FY28, within a broader plan to set up 100,000 MTPA capacity in phases from early 2027. Ahead of Phase I, the Company upgraded existing Pharma and Food Iron Phosphate capacity to produce 5,000 MT of battery-grade material and has secured commercial purchase orders against this upgraded capacity. Current overall capacity utilisation across the Company's manufacturing facilities is close to 50%, with the Pharma, Food & Nutrition vertical operating at ~65% against an optimum utilisation of ~70%. Management's stated priorities for FY 2026-27 are to ramp the Nandesari facility through customer qualification, increase utilisation and deepen integration at NSS, sustain momentum in Specialty Ingredients (particularly North America and Europe), and carry Sudeep Advanced Materials through validation towards commissioning.
currentContext.mdna: Customers in regulated pharmaceutical and nutrition markets increasingly value supply security, technical depth and regulatory credibility over price alone, and manufacturers are diversifying sourcing away from single-geography dependence — structural shifts management believes favour Sudeep's capabilities.|NSS (Ireland) currently operates at only around a third of its capacity; Sudeep India is becoming its primary ingredient supplier, which management expects to improve supply visibility and strengthen margins across the chain — framed as embedded operating leverage with room for growth.|Price increases on key inputs such as phosphoric acid were passed through only from the start of FY 2026-27, so the associated margin benefit is expected to show in coming quarters.|The Pharmaceutical, Food & Nutrition vertical had been running close to optimal capacity, capping growth; the new Nandesari facility is expected to remove that constraint and support larger off-take agreements and scaling of higher-value molecules (gluconates, glycinates).|AbsorBis (bisglycinate ingredients) addresses a roughly US$1 Billion global category at materially higher realisation than the core portfolio — an early but important growth contributor.|In Battery Materials, the commercial signal is described as increasingly measurable, based on active engagement across the cathode, cell, EV and energy-storage customer ecosystem at varying stages of validation.|FY 2025-26 was a challenging operating environment: gas supply disruptions, sharp increases in phosphoric and sulphuric acid prices, and logistics pressures.|New US tariffs announced in August 2025 caused several customers to pause and assess impact before ordering patterns normalised; the Company responded by keeping supply dependable and planning inventory jointly with customers.|Battery Materials: engaged with 42 customers across the cathode, cell, EV and energy-storage ecosystem; of these, 22 are in lab validation, 14 in pilot-scale evaluation, and six have completed commercial validation and are in active off-take talks.|Battery Materials has already received around 700 MT of initial commercial orders, being serviced by upgrading an existing pharma line ahead of Phase 1.|Specialty Ingredients: now supplies the world's largest bakery in encapsulation and has won approvals with two further top-five global players; approved by the world's largest infant-nutrition company in premixes.

risks.note: US tariffs introduced in August 2025 led some customers to adopt a cautious approach and initially slowed procurement. Management states 50% of the US business is now tariff-exempt, and for the remaining business ~90% of the cost impact has been passed on to customers, but exposure to further trade-policy shifts remains a watch item.

Specialised segments such as clinical and infant nutrition carry high entry barriers and long regulatory approval cycles of around 4-7 years; the Company has sought to shortcut this via the NSS (Ireland) acquisition, but the underlying regulatory-timeline risk for organic expansion into new regulated markets persists.
The Company depends on a select group of customers, with the top 10 customers contributing 40.78% of revenue in FY 2024-25, creating exposure to loss of, or reduced demand from, any large account.

risks.risk: Raw material price and availability risk
risks.note: The Company is exposed to price fluctuations and availability risk in key raw materials including phosphoric acid and mineral calcium, which can pressure margins if not passed through to customers.

Inventory days increased as the Company built higher stock levels in international markets to support new long-term contracts and new warehousing in the US, Spain and the Netherlands; management expects rotation and stabilisation to improve inventory holding days in FY 2026-27, but elevated working capital remains a near-term drag.

risks.risk: Financial and market risk (forex / interest rate)
risks.note: The Company is exposed to foreign exchange fluctuations and interest-rate risk on floating-rate borrowings, managed via natural hedges, forward contracts and interest rate swaps.

Three of the Company's four legacy manufacturing facilities are located in Vadodara, Gujarat, creating exposure to regional disruptions; the Company is diversifying its footprint through the NSS facility in Ireland and the upcoming Dahej, Gujarat plant (which itself remains within the same state).

one-line thesis: Strong Q3FY26 growth (52% revenue, 66% PAT) driven by specialty ingredients (41% revenue) and battery-grade iron phosphate traction, with new capacity (Nandesari Greenfield, Dahej) on track to unlock scalable, high-margin volume from H2FY27; what matters is the transition from commodity excipient supplier to strategic partner in regulated global supply chains with battery materials as a multi-year growth lever.
financial scorecard: revenue: +52% YoY to INR179.2cr (ex-NSS: +35.3% YoY); EBITDA: +60% YoY to INR66.8cr, margin: 37.3% (ex-NSS: 35-37%); PAT: +66% YoY to INR47.7cr (rptd); order book: 34 active battery customers with 70% sample approval; net debt: financed via internal accruals, no significant interest impact expected until FY28
guidance: revenue growth: sustain 35-40% CAGR; margin: maintain 35-38% EBITDA margin; order inflow: scaling specialty ingredients (70-80% util. in 2 yrs); capex/commissioning: Nandesari Greenfield (51.2k tons) commissioning Q4FY26 (Mar'26); Dahej Battery Phase 1 (25k tons) commissioning early 2027; total battery capex INR550-600cr
order book & pipeline: 34 global battery customers engaged; 70% have approved samples; commercial-scale pilot orders already received; off-take agreements under active negotiation
segment / subsidiary detail: Pharma/Food & Nutrition: 59% of Q3 revenue; calcium portfolio core; Europe growth accelerating with CEP certification; Specialty Ingredients: 41% of Q3 revenue; encapsulated/premixed lines growing with new wins (tortilla giant, global FMCG); NSS acquisition contributing INR17cr revenue, margins aligned to Sudeep core
growth verticals / optionality: Battery-grade iron phosphate (Dahej) to scale to 100k tons by FY28; Nandesari Greenfield enabling gluconates/glycinates/citrates; liposomal tech (Lipoboost) to launch H2FY27 with clinical validation; NSS integration unlocking infant nutrition segment
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 37.3% in Q3; maintained despite NSS integration; green chemistry reduces opex vs China; battery margins expected to exceed industry average; no margin dilution from US tariffs (90% passed on)
capex / expansion: Total capex: INR550-600cr for 100k ton battery facility (Dahej); INR150cr for Nandesari Greenfield (mostly spent); no major capex planned for core or specialty segments beyond this
capital allocation: Funding via internal accruals; no significant debt expected until FY28; prioritizing high-ROCE battery and specialty platforms over commodity expansion
risks & watch-items: Execution delays in commissioning; customer approval lags for new facilities; geopolitical volatility in export markets; battery material pricing competition
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, execution-focused; emphasizing differentiated tech, ex-China positioning, and long-term partnerships; no revenue guidance but clear intent to sustain 35-40% growth
non-obvious takeaways: Liposomal iron and vitamin C show 80% higher absorption vs conventional; green chemistry reduces waste and capex vs Chinese rivals; NSS acquisition is not just revenue add but margin enhancer via vertical integration

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
